This session's stated ruling ('D11/D12 stand') leaves D11 -- and DECISIONS.md's own §6 override text -- exactly as written, i.e. it does not ratify the widening. The fix round did not attempt to code around this (correctly: 'ADV-655-7 was deliberately answered with a comment rather than a code gate for exactly that reason'), and named it prominently in three places (migration header MEASUREMENT 2, 655-final.md's 'Scope deviation' section, and this round's own report). ratification_requests_judged.judgment: Unlike F1, this is NOT a violation of the literal brief: brief-655.md's section 4 cell 11 prescribes `posting_date + 30` verbatim, and the shipped `clara._trade_invoice_due` does exactly that (measured: document_date 2026-03-04, posting_date 2026-03-31, terms 30 days -> due_date 2026-04-30, confirmed via the now-un-vacuumed p655.parity.source_vs_direct cell, which pins the number by name and asserts the 27-day gap is real, not vacuous). D12's own text ('到期日单据写的优先、账期兜底' -- the document-stated due date wins, payment-terms is the FALLBACK) settles the priority between a STATED due date and a terms-derived one, but does not itself say what the terms fallback should anchor ON (document date vs. posting date) -- so D12 does not resolve this question either way, and this session's 'D11/D12 stand' ruling leaves that silence in place rather than closing it. The fix round correctly declined to change behaviour that matches the brief's literal text, and instead made the number impossible to miss (the pinned assertion reds the moment either the brief or the code changes). This is a genuine accounting-correctness concern worth an owner ruling (payment terms conventionally run from the document, and `document_date` was added by this very ticket), but it is not a shipped deviation from what was asked for the way F1 is.
ratification_requests_judged.recommendation: orchestrator should rule on the anchor when convenient; not blocking, since the current code does what brief-655.md literally specifies and the disagreement is measured and cannot silently drift
